title: The Brothers' War Retro Artifacts: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: While most power is used for ordinary, everyday tasks, one shouldn't underestimate its potential for the extraordinary.
"It is not that you will go mad. It is that you will beg for madness." —Volrath
"If you work at sawing up carcasses, you notice how the joints fit, how the nerves are arrayed, and how the skin peels back." —Ashnod, to Tawnos
It spilled the blood of one elder dragon. In Gideon's hands, it may yet taste another's.
In a world where death is always violent, cruel weapons are as common as rocks.
Forged by divine hands to wander mortal realms.
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.
The musical sound of its turning triggers the tumblers of revelation.
It lights up the sky, beckoning enemies only to repel them.
Only a monster could create such a door. Only a fool would open it.
One night Oona bottled the sky. The next night she aligned the stars and released it.
Automaton inspectors ensure that the Consulate's stringent standards for mass production are upheld.
"The perfection of the lotus reminds me of my hopes for this world . . . and my failures. I will not rest until I've atoned for them." —Karn
The mine's riches never end, nor do the moans of the spirits doomed to haunt them.
"Our glorious infection has taken hold." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
Ghirapur's most celebrated inventors have been immortalized in clockwork.
Valuing scholarship above all else, the inhabitants of the Ivory Tower reward those who sacrifice power for knowledge.
Most books simply deliver knowledge. This one expects some in return.
"From the clouds, you can see as far as the distant horizon. It's a reminder of the infinite possibilities of everyday life." —Noboru, master kitemaker
As it spins, dead voices shriek in an ever-increasing cacophony, rending the mind asunder.
It would be unfortunate if the key fell into the wrong hands.
"They'll soon become accustomed to wearing skin that is not their own." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
"Somehow it warps the Æther. It brings a strange weight, a blockade in the flow of spellcraft." —Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
A step in one direction is two steps away from another.
Minds, like mountains, are never so grand and mighty that they can't be reduced to dust.
"Ideas drift like petals on the wind. I have only to lift my face to the breeze."
"Arcum is a babbling fool! Phyrexian technology is our greatest blessing. Take this delightful trinket for instance . . ." —Heidar, Rimewind master
A moment in time made tangible, it has the power to realize epic visions.
Once a year, the skies over Paliano fill with the flying machines of those who hope to be taken on as pupils by the artificer Muzzio.
The spirit dragon Ugin arranged the hedrons of Zendikar to direct leylines of energy. To disrupt one is to unleash devastation and chaos.
"To be in the presence of a revoker is to be truly alone." —Kara Vrist, Neurok agent
She is the apex of the artificer's craft, the spirit of the divine called out of base metal.
"Tools and artisans can be destroyed, but the act of creation is inviolate." —Elspeth Tirel
"If that brain can't figure out the secret of the serum, then add more brains." —Rhmir, Hand of the Augur
Those who examine the amulet too closely have been known to become part of its ornate carvings.
As sharp as its bearer's words of faith.
An artificer once dropped one in a vault full of coins. She has yet to find it.
It sees itself in all of its creations.
Forged from what it forges.
With each honor he earns, Gideon paves the path to his redemption.
"The music is in the drum. I simply coax it out to be heard."
"Even if we defeat it, what remains to be saved?" —Glissa Sunseeker
"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared." —Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
Mined from a cave in the Dark Meanders, it shines brightest when no one is looking.
"The partisans have unearthed a strange artifact. None know its origin, but it gives them hope of a life beyond." —Elspeth's journal
Some say the knowledge lost during the Ritual of Rebuking is returned through the well's waters.
"These estimates are conservative. Its true capacity may be far, far greater." —Research notes, signature illegible
"My dreams have brought more visions from our master: an altar, exquisite and perfect. We must build it at once." —Writings of Artonac, priest of Gix
"Blood fluting needs to be deeper. Additional hooks needed for nerve rigging. Surface stippling could be coarser." —Ashnod, design notes
"Tempered in the blood of ten thousand sacrifices? Superstitious drivel." —Mishra, note to his researchers
"When metal instruments are scarce, a saw constructed from the subject's femur will suffice for a craniectomy." —Ashnod, research notes
"The natural world has already solved our problems. Our challenge is to replicate the elegance of its solutions." —Tawnos
"Feldon's latest discovery appears to draw upon the same 'memories of the land' my wife studied. How I wish she could see it." —Writings of Drafna
"A key only unlocks a door. Its wielder must choose whether to cross the threshold." —*Hurkyl's Metaphysics, vol. II*
"Properly installed, each powerstone emits a targeted electromagnetic field that halts momentum as sure as stone." —*Tome of Obstructions*
"I have re-created a Thran portal at last! Before I inform Lord Urza, I'll test it myself." —Oryan, Urzan artificer, final research note
"My husband is clever enough to bottle the sky, and foolish enough to ignore its beauty." —Queen Kayla bin-Kroog
"Delicate resonance detectors could scan the assembly lines for metallic impurities, loose bolts, and freak occurrences of sentience." —Tawnos, proposal for overseer prototype
"The lotus is a potent but ephemeral source of power. To preserve its potency, lacquer carefully with a conductive coating." —*Hurkyl's Metaphysics, vol. II*
"The Sardian dwarves have let superstition override common sense. There's plenty of ore left in the mountain, and we mustn't let it go to waste." —Last dispatch of Bolgon, Argivian surveyor
"Should a single drop take hold, the oil begins to consume organic tissue and will multiply until it overwhelms the host." —Yawgmoth, collected writings
"In the early days, Urza's wondrous automatons were seen as symbols of hope and courage." —*The Antiquities War*
"Ringed by white stone, Terisia was a city of scholarship and knowledge, where magic promised a brighter future to a world devoured by artifice." —*The Antiquities War*
"These glyphs describe a Thran device capable of controlling a machine army, but the dimensions make no sense. It's nearly the size of the Null Moon." —Urza, diary
"Measure the angles carefully. Note the gauge of the paper. By your sixth birthday, I expect a flying prototype." —Tawnos, letter to Harbin
"The new prototype utilizing a rotational axis is marvelously effective: it makes me want to tear my own ears off." —Ashnod, to her assistants
"Presented to the Chief Artificer in recognition of his unparalleled service to Yotia." —Rusted plaque
"We've had a breakthrough on the fifth iteration. The subject's skin was entirely replaced within an hour, and he survived a full day after that!" —Ashnod, to Mishra
"Progress update: the problem of the slagheap blocking the entrance seems to have solved itself." —Mine supervisor's report
"I now believe the strange orb was some kind of Thran security device. Supporting this theory, I can no longer recall where I found it." —Tocasia, journal entry
"In the lean months, communities lived off a bitterwheat berry so tough that its flour contained more millstone than grain." —*On the Early History of Keld*
"I sit and I think of Lat-Nam, of the azure waves white with froth, suspended over the shore. I see the energy there and I call it here." —Hurkyl, meditation notes
"The secrets of my great-uncle's heirloom lie in the world where it was forged: the grease-stained wastes of Phyrexia." —Jarsyl, diary
"A crystallized moment in time from the Mending Era, first discovered during the Ice Age. A temporal conundrum, even to the great scholar himself." —*The Discoveries of Feldon*

"Without Urza's ingenuity, the wings would never have borne weight. Without Mishra's courage, we would never have known the machine's true potential. I hope this persuades them to work together more." —Tocasia, journal entry
"As the years passed, Urza turned his focus from the Thran to worlds beyond his own, seeking any spell or technology that might break the Phyrexian scourge." —*Urza: From Prodigy to Planeswalker*
"These skittering creatures were created to hunt the one true threat to Phyrexia: dissent." —Venser, journal
"Serra built angels from the spirits of fallen warriors, but I believe a more mundane power source might suffice." —Karn
"A rakalite core paired with a powerstone matrix has significantly increased the healing effects of my original amulet design." —Urza, research notes
"Perhaps drawing the impossible monster will lessen the burden my memory must bear." —Jarsyl, diary
"If powerstones are energy stored in material form, could we store matter as energy in the same way?" —Rayne, research notes
"Harmonic resonance infusions amplify the natural abilities of the song mages of Sumifa." —Drafna, research notes
"Based on his early work with primal clay, Tawnos refined the rare metals in the earth into self-assembling strands." —*After the War*
"Test 37: Sentience module is still too strong. It's adding ears again." —Development log of Willa, Yotian artificer
"The forges consumed all and still screamed for more." —*The Antiquities War*
"This war will be over quickly, so we can afford to make the medals out of gold." —Dispatch from the Merchant Council of Korlis
"It is neither the species of leaf nor the thickness of branch that creates music. Gaea's song is already in the drum." —Gamelen, Citanul elder
"Give the schematic to the younger brother. Tell him that it will surely keep Argoth's resources out of Urza's hands." —Gix, Yawgmoth praetor
"Test 12: Boots now protect wearer from all hazards except blisters. Need to source better insoles." —Development log of Willa, Yotian artificer
"The geode must be mined in moonlight and broken open by a silver hammer." —*Tome of Obstructions*
"Heat from the rotating mechanism is captured and converted into energy, allowing it to operate in perpetuity." —*Rusko's Compendium of Clockwork*
"A wish can be controlled. Dreams are far more chaotic, and ungoverned by rationale." —*Hurkyl's Metaphysics, vol. II*
